summary: Ariel Shapiro's Hot Pod newsletter for The Verge examines Spotify's Q3 2023 earnings, where an 'efficiency' focus and AI tools replaced the earlier emphasis on original podcast content. It also covers Wondery launching three channels on Amazon's Freevee and PodBam's list of the most-searched podcasts, led by The Joe Rogan Experience.
one_line: Spotify's efficiency-driven earnings emphasize AI translation and ads over original podcasts, while Wondery heads to Freevee and Joe Rogan tops podcast searches.
key_facts: Spotify reported an operating profit for the first time in a year, and the stock rose nearly 10 percent.
The revenue bump was largely due to Spotify's $1 price increase earlier in 2023, though executives also credited downsizing the podcast operation.
The podcast downsizing included hundreds of layoffs and the dissolution of Gimlet and Parcast.
CFO Paul Vogel said podcasting, previously a 'drag' on profit margins, will soon break even and turn toward profitability.
Ek and Vogel said 'efficiency' more than 30 times during the 50-minute investor call, according to the author's transcript.
CEO Daniel Ek highlighted Spotify's AI-driven automatic podcast translation tool as a way to scale content in non-English speaking markets.
Ek said generative AI could cut audio ad creative costs and enable 1,000, 10,000 or even 100,000 ads individually created for each user.
The author wonders how licensing deals with Joe Rogan, Alex Cooper and Dax Shepard will fit in as they come up for renewal.
On October 31st, Freevee will launch three Wondery channels: a flagship entertainment channel, Exhibit C for true crime, and Wondery Sports.
Wondery and Freevee (formerly IMDb TV) are both owned by Amazon, so the author sees little risk in the strategy but doubts it is replicable beyond Amazon.
Wondery's Freevee channels will feature shows including Baby, This is Keke Palmer, Business Wars, American Scandal, Dr. Death, Morbid, Don't Call It a Comeback and Gladiator.
PodBam's list of the 40 most-searched podcasts put The Joe Rogan Experience first with 135,000 average monthly Google searches, followed by Call Her Daddy (106,000) and This American Life (81,000).
